profile.headline: Software Engineer III  at LexisNexis Risk Solutions
profile.summary:
I am a software engineer with a passion for game design. I graduated from a top 10 Princeton Reviewed school for Video Game Engineering, Shawnee State University, with a Bachelors in Software Engineering and Digital Simulation, with a focus on Video Game Engineering. I am currently employed as a .NET developer.

I am currently employed with LexisNexis Risk in Oklahoma City. I am a .NET developer on their Traffic department, working primarily on C# and Python applications. I am currently the Scrum Master of my team, where my weekly responsibilities include: leading weekly grooming meetings to plan out the development work of my team, communicating with the Business Unit to make sure development efforts are inline with the business goals, and helping design tools and applications that will help increase the speed and efficiency of daily operations.

I have over 5 years experience using Unity3D, having deployed games for browsers, Android, iOS, and PC-standalone. Several of these projects were created to be integrated with a VR system, in some cases several VR systems. I am proficient in Python and C#. I am partial to using Python 3, I have also used Python 2 for its legacy libraries, and am currently engaged with .NET.

I was also the lead Unity Developer for Lantern Light Studios: http://lanternlightstudios.com/. I played a large role in helping release their first title "Gloobs" in Dec 2016 and helped lay the framework on their second project. Gloobs was released for Android and iOS with a port to PC,  while the second project was developed for a Steam release.

positions.title: Scrum Master
positions.description: Plan the work for a team of Software Engineers so that we are meeting business goals and management expectations to keep our current projects on track and our work focused. Manage bi-weekly sprints based on team capacity, plan work for future sprints, and continuously update items in the backlog to keep up with upcoming projects. At the end of every sprint, put together a presentation to update stakeholders and project owners on team progress and impediments.

positions.title: Game Programmer
positions.description: Mobile game developer at LLS. Environment used is Unity 5.3. Current project is Gloobs. Will update with more details at end of project.

positions.title: Contract Software Engineer
positions.description: Contracted to Lexis Nexis - Risk in Oklahoma City starting Sept 2017 as a C# dev.

positions.title: Technical Support Specialist
positions.description:
Responded to customer inquiries concerning the various products offered by YEI Technology. Some of the tasks that I took care of on a weekly basis included:
-Produce, package, and test products for their Kickstarter Project, PrioVR.
-Update backers and general public about PrioVR via bi-weekly status updates.
-Gained an intimate knowledge of all YEI 3-Space products.
-Gained experience with scripting and commanding 3-Space sensors through serial protocol
-Calibrate, Test, and trouble shoot all forms of 3-Space Sensors (http://www.yeitechnology.com/3-space-product-family)
-Gained experience writing professional emails, for both client contacts and support.

positions.title: Content Developer Programmer
positions.description:
Worked on the team for the PrioVR kickstarter project (http://tinyurl.com/nhqxnkv). I was part of the small content team in charge of creating demos that showed off the suits capabilities. I worked on creating game mechanics that made use of the suits full body tracking features. The mechanics ranged from guns and archery to sports-like tasks such as throwing and kicking to casting spells as a wizard. Each demo at this point was scripted using C# and was made in Unity3D.

Notable Achievements:
- Designed the system for casting spells that was used in the final implementation of the Wizard Demo
- Demos were made to work in conjunction with the Oculus Rift, while also supporting the PrioVR
- Created the foundation for the CopyCat (Dancing) demo game. This includes scene structure, level loading, player data retention, and persistence of data of peripheral devices (Oculus, PrioVR, 3-Space Mocap Suit, etc.)
- Created mechanics for the Archery Tech Demo. This includes visual projection of arrow launch, realistic forces of arrow firing, bullet collision, and 2 different game modes.

projects.title: Pure
projects.description:
Pure is a relaxation-based mobile platform game. It was designed and prototyped in less than a month  as part of the Ohio University Game Dev, Shape Jam. Current builds exists for PC, Web Player, and Android.Work is still ongoing on Pure, with additional levels, mechanics, and assets on the way.

My responsibilities were to program the game. It was made using Unity 5.1 and C#. Weekly prints with set milestones were met each week, and progress was measured in playability.

projects.title: Metarcade - Indies Vs Gamers 2015
projects.description:
A small side scrolling bullet hell. Three levels of lazer-y goodness.The game was completed within 72 hours.

My responsibilities included creating the menus, the weapon systems, the scene flow, the power-ups, and integrating the GameJolt API. I also made a lot of the 2D art for the menus. I did some work on the enemies, although that was primarily completed by Nick Leyder.

Joining the game jam was my suggestion, so I gathered the the majority of the team members, and organized the group. The game was hosted is hosted on my GameJolt account.
